evidence_cards.content: A JU may have the capability to purge remote tracks/points, i.e., automatically drop a remote track/point after a specified time interval has elapsed since the track's/point's last report.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This sentence defines the objective of the 'Purging' use case: to remove stale data (remote tracks/points) that have not been updated within a specific timeframe.

evidence_cards.content: The transmission of EW product information shall be terminated when the information is no longer valid or time-related update requirements are not met.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the high-level objective and condition for terminating surveillance data transmission.

evidence_cards.content: A JU may have the capability to purge remote tracks/points.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes that the ability to perform the purge action is a conditional capability ('may have') rather than a guaranteed state, serving as a precondition for the use case.

evidence_cards.content: A system may not receive a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message and receives no further updates on the remote track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This state represents the specific condition under which the automatic purging of remote tracks is triggered, serving as a precondition for the purge action.

evidence_cards.content: The system has received remote ballistic missile tracks that have not been terminated by a J7.0 message with the Track Management Action field set to value 0 (Drop Track Report).

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies the condition where data flow has stopped, which is required before the time-based purge mechanism can be evaluated.

evidence_cards.content: The system must have existing remote surveillance tracks or points that are being monitored (specifically by nonC2 JUs) and for which update requirements may no longer be met.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes the existence of the data entities (remote tracks/points) required for the termination and purge process to occur.

evidence_cards.content: A specified time interval parameter must be defined in the system design to determine when locally held remote tracks should be automatically purged if they are no longer being updated.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies a necessary configuration state (the 'specified time interval') that must exist before the automatic purge capability can function.

evidence_cards.content: The trigger for purging is the automatic dropping of a remote track/point after a specified time interval has elapsed since the track's/point's last report.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This sentence explicitly defines the event (elapsed time since last report) that initiates the automatic purge action by the JU.

evidence_cards.content: The J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is transmitted when a JU ceases reporting a track for which it currently has R², except in specific cases such as relinquishing R² to another JU or the track becoming an Active IU on the network.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the triggering event for terminating transmission of EW product information: the cessation of reporting by the JU, which initiates the drop track report process.

evidence_cards.content: There may be cases when a system does not receive a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message and receives no further updates on the remote track, requiring each system to have its own mechanism for purging stale tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes the trigger condition for automatic purging of remote tracks — absence of both explicit termination messages and subsequent updates — which starts the purge use case.

evidence_cards.content: The trigger for terminating a track occurs when a JU ceases reporting a track (except when that track becomes an active IU on the network with the same address as was previously being used as the reference TN), or at the time of deactivation for NOTACK areas, Moving Havens, and FWDAs.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the specific events (ceasing reporting or deactivation) that initiate the termination process.

evidence_cards.content: The trigger for purging remote tracks occurs when a system does not receive a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message and receives no further updates on the remote track, resulting in the elapse of a specific time interval since the last report.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the condition (timeout due to lack of updates) that initiates the automatic purge process.

evidence_cards.content: The trigger for purging remote ballistic missile tracks is the case when a system does not receive a J7.0 message with the Track Management Action field set to value 0 (Drop Track Report) and receives no further updates on the remote ballistic missile track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies the specific event conditions (missing drop message and lack of updates) that start the purge process for remote tracks.

evidence_cards.content: The trigger for terminating transmission of a ballistic missile track report is when a JU ceases reporting a ballistic missile track for which it currently has R², except when relinquishing R² to another JU.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the exact condition under which the termination of track data transmission begins.

evidence_cards.content: The JU automatically drops a remote track/point after a specified time interval has elapsed since the track's/point's last report.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the primary step in the main flow for purging stale remote tracks/points.

evidence_cards.content: The JU shall not transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message on a purged remote track/point.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies a constraint during the execution of the purge action in the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: When a JU ceases reporting a track because it has relinquished R² to another JU, or when that track becomes an Active IU on the network with the same TN, the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message shall not be transmitted.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines specific exceptions in the main flow where the termination message is suppressed despite the trigger condition being met.

evidence_cards.content: The system must have the capability to automatically purge tracks after a specific time interval if no J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is received and no further updates occur; under this condition, a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message shall not be transmitted.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the automatic purging mechanism as part of the main flow for handling stale remote tracks without explicit termination messages.

evidence_cards.content: When a JU ceases reporting a track (except when it becomes an active IU on the network with the same address), the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is transmitted to terminate the subsurface track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the specific system action (transmission of termination message) in response to the actor ceasing to report, constituting the main flow for track termination.

evidence_cards.content: For NOTACK areas, Moving Havens, and FWDAs, a J7.0 (ACT=0) message shall be transmitted at the time of deactivation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the exact interaction sequence (message transmission) required by the system when the trigger condition (deactivation) occurs for specific entity types.

evidence_cards.content: The J7.0 message with the Track Management Action field set to value 0, Drop Track Report, is transmitted when a JU ceases reporting a ballistic missile track for which it currently has R², except when a JU ceases reporting a track because it has relinquished R² to another JU.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the primary action in the main flow for terminating a local ballistic missile track by transmitting a specific drop report message.

evidence_cards.content: Each system should have the capability to automatically purge remote ballistic missile tracks after a specific time interval if it does not receive a J7.0 message with the Track Management Action field set to value 0 and receives no further updates on the track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the automatic purging mechanism for remote tracks that are no longer being updated, which constitutes the main flow for handling stale data without an explicit drop message.

evidence_cards.content: The transmission of EW product information shall be terminated when the information is no longer valid or time-related update requirements are not met.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the core action for terminating EW product data in the main flow based on validity and update status.

evidence_cards.content: When a JU drops or ceases reporting EW information that it has been reporting on the interface, it shall transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the specific message transmission required to terminate local EW reporting.

evidence_cards.content: Remote reports may be automatically purged based on system criteria.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the automated purge mechanism for remote reports as part of the termination process.

evidence_cards.content: A change from live to simulated simulation status shall be accepted if the track is being received from an FJU, which is an exception to the general rule that the Simulation Indicator shall not change and that a track must be dropped using J7.0 (ACT = 0) before reporting a new track when changing simulation status.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes a legal alternative path for handling simulation status changes — specifically allowing a direct transition from live to simulated without dropping and re-reporting the track, provided the source is an FJU. This diverges from the main flow’s requirement to drop and re-report when changing simulation status due to operator error or other reasons.

evidence_cards.content: A JU does not transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message when it ceases reporting a track if it has relinquished R² to another JU.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a successful alternative path for track termination where the standard Drop Track message is suppressed because responsibility was transferred.

evidence_cards.content: A JU does not transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message when it ceases reporting a track if that track becomes an Active IU on the network with the same TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a successful alternative path for track termination where the standard Drop Track message is suppressed due to the track's status change to Active IU.

evidence_cards.content: For ASW points NOTACK Area, Moving Haven, and FWDA, if both activation and deactivation times are not received, the default period for NOTACK Areas is 2 hours and for FWDAs is 155 minutes.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This provides a specific alternative flow for handling missing time data (a divergence from the standard requirement to report times) that still results in successful processing of the track/point with a default value.

evidence_cards.content: For Sonobuoy Position and Sonobuoy Pattern Reference Position, if the time of deactivation is not reported, the time of activation may be reported instead to specify the time for the deployment of future assets.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes an alternative reporting path where the expected 'deactivation' trigger is replaced by an 'activation' parameter to achieve the goal of specifying asset timing.

evidence_cards.content: When a JU ceases reporting a track (except when that track becomes an active IU on the network with the same address as was previously being used as the reference TN), it transmits a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message to terminate the subsurface track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes an alternative successful path for terminating tracks — diverging from the main flow’s automatic purge by explicit termination via J7.0 message when the track is relinquished or transitions to another IU, which is a valid variant of track termination under the use case.

evidence_cards.content: For NOTACK areas, Moving Havens, and FWDAs, a J7.0 (ACT=0) message shall be transmitted at time of deactivation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies an additional alternative flow condition where termination occurs not due to staleness but due to area deactivation — a distinct trigger leading to successful termination via J7.0 message, qualifying as an alternative success path.

evidence_cards.content: A JU receiving a J7.0 message with the Track Management Action field set to value 0 (Drop Track Report) on a locally held track shall assume R² at the next opportunity to transmit the track if local reporting eligibility remains and a remote report has not been received on that track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes an alternative successful path where instead of dropping/terminating a track upon receipt of a J7.0 Drop command, the JU assumes responsibility (R²) for it under specific conditions — diverging from the main flow’s automatic drop action when no updates are received.

evidence_cards.content: A JU without R² for a nonreal-time track (TQ field set to value 0) shall assume R² for that track when the track is locally updated by a new nonreal-time report; a JU reporting a nonreal-time track has R² regardless of the time value in the track report, and the time value in a nonreal-time report is not a criterion for an R² shift.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines an alternative success scenario for nonreal-time tracks where R² assumption occurs based on local update rather than time-based purge or termination criteria — diverging from the main flow’s reliance on elapsed time intervals or validity checks.

evidence_cards.content: A JU relinquishes R² for a real-time track upon reception of a remote track report with TQ greater than local TQ.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies an alternative successful divergence point: instead of retaining or purging a track based on staleness, the JU actively relinquishes responsibility upon receiving a higher-quality remote report — altering the main flow’s passive timeout-based termination logic.

evidence_cards.content: After applying all above rules, a JU relinquishes R² for a real-time track upon reception of a remote track report with TQ equal to the local TQ from a JU whose Source TN is greater than the local Source TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This provides another alternative success path where R² is relinquished based on source priority (Source TN) when quality (TQ) is tied — again diverging from the main flow’s time-based or validity-based termination triggers.

evidence_cards.content: A unit assuming R² for a ballistic missile track need not assume R² for the associated launch point; the unit no longer holding R² on the ballistic missile track may continue to report the launch point in accordance with transmit/receive rules.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes an alternative successful outcome where partial responsibility retention (launch point only) is permitted after relinquishing R² for the primary track — diverging from the main flow’s full termination/purge behavior.

evidence_cards.content: A J7.0 (ACT = 0) message shall not be sent when a track is no longer being reported due to a shift in R².
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines an alternative flow for terminating a track where the standard 'Drop Track Report' message is explicitly suppressed because the cessation of reporting is caused by a change in R² rather than a manual drop or timeout.

evidence_cards.content: If for any reason, such as operator error, it is desired to change the simulation status of a track (e.g., from live to simulated), the standard rule that the Simulation Indicator shall not change has an exception: the track shall be dropped using the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message, and a new track shall be reported.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This provides a specific exception flow where an error condition (operator error requiring a status change) forces the system to deviate from the normal 'do not change' rule by terminating the current track and starting a new one.

evidence_cards.content: When a system does not receive a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message and receives no further updates on the remote track, it shall have the capability to automatically purge those tracks after a specific time interval.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the exception condition (missing termination message + no updates) that triggers automatic purging as an alternative to explicit termination signaling.

evidence_cards.content: Under the condition where a system automatically purges a remote track due to missing J7.0 (ACT = 0) and no further updates, a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message shall not be transmitted.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the exit path constraint for this exception flow — no termination message is sent when purging occurs automatically due to absence of update/termination signal.

evidence_cards.content: DATUMS (DRT = 4) shall not be purged automatically.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception to the automatic purge flow: DATUMS are explicitly excluded from being dropped by the system after a time interval, requiring different handling than other remote tracks.

evidence_cards.content: Receiving JUs which do not implement the changed Environment/Category and have R² on the track must cease reporting the track and transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception flow where a receiving JU encounters a capability mismatch (missing implementation of Environment/Category change) while holding R², requiring it to terminate reporting and send a specific termination message rather than processing the order normally.

evidence_cards.content: JUs shall not transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 2) message containing an ID of Pending.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies a constraint that prevents the transmission of a Change Data Order if the ID is in a 'Pending' state, acting as an exception condition for initiating the data change process.

evidence_cards.content: Units receiving a J7.0 (ACT = 2) Change Data Order message containing an ID of Pending shall not accept that order.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the exception handling path for a receiving unit when it receives a Change Data Order with an invalid or pending ID, resulting in the rejection of the order.

evidence_cards.content: If a selection conflict occurs due to OCCs on both the Retained TN and the Dropped TN during dual designation determination, the correlation shall be abandoned until the next correlation check.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception path for the Terminate and Purge Surveillance Tracks use case where track termination via correlation fails due to conflicting operational control conditions (OCCs), resulting in abandonment rather than immediate action.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs receiving a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 0 or 1 shall not accept the requested correlation when local or remote data held indicates there is a correlation restriction as listed in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1g; in this case the correlation shall be rejected.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies an explicit rejection condition (exception flow) for the track termination/correlation process based on existing system restrictions.

evidence_cards.content: The remote track/point has been automatically dropped (purged) from the system.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes the resulting state of the data object after the purge trigger and action are completed successfully.

evidence_cards.content: No J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is transmitted on the interface for the purged remote track/point.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the specific communication state of the system following a successful purge operation, distinguishing it from explicit termination actions.

evidence_cards.content: The remote track/point is dropped from the system without the transmission of a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the observable system state after the automatic purge trigger elapses: the data is removed silently.

evidence_cards.content: A J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is transmitted on the interface to terminate the track when C2 JU ceases reporting it (except in specific cases like relinquishing R² or the track becoming an Active IU).

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the observable system state after the explicit termination action: the track is terminated via a specific message transmission.

evidence_cards.content: After successful completion of the use case, the remote track/point has been automatically purged from the system (DRT = 0-3) and is no longer held locally.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the resulting system state for the purge branch: the stale data is removed.

evidence_cards.content: For a purged remote track/point, no J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is transmitted to the network.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the resulting interface state for the purge branch: silence on the network regarding this specific track termination.

evidence_cards.content: The transmission of EW product information (subsurface tracks) has been terminated via the transmission of a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message on the interface.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the resulting interface state for the termination branch: an explicit drop message has been sent.

evidence_cards.content: The transmission of EW product information is terminated, and the information may be purged in accordance with system design.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the final state of the EW product information (transmission stopped, data potentially removed) after the termination criteria are met.

evidence_cards.content: Remote reports may be automatically purged based on system criteria.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes that the postcondition for remote reports involves automatic removal from the system based on defined criteria.

evidence_cards.content: For remotely reported tracks that are purged (dropped due to lack of updates), a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is not transmitted.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies a critical constraint on the system's output state: the absence of a termination message distinguishes an automatic purge from an active drop.

evidence_cards.content: NonC² JUs process J7.0 messages with Track Management Action set to value 0 (Drop Track Report) for locally held remote tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Confirms that upon receipt of the drop command, the local state of the remote track is updated/removed via processing.

evidence_cards.content: Upon receipt of the J7.0 (ACT = 3 or 4) message terminating the alert, all receiving JUs shall terminate the alert in their databases.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the postcondition for the termination of EW product information alerts: the system state changes such that receiving nodes have removed the alert from their databases.

evidence_cards.content: Optionally, alerts may be cleared by reception of a J3.7 message with the EMG IND and/or FT IND set to value 0.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes an alternative mechanism for achieving the postcondition where the alert indicator is explicitly reset to 0 in the database.

evidence_cards.content: When a transmit filter is activated by a unit, the unit shall cease reporting any track for which it has R² and which meets the filter criteria.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific system state change (cessation of reporting) that occurs as a result of filter activation, contributing to the postconditions of terminating track transmission.

evidence_cards.content: The unit shall comply with the rules for terminating transmission of the applicable track data of the applicable Environment/Category when a transmit filter is activated.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes that the system enters a state where transmission termination rules are actively being followed for filtered tracks.

evidence_cards.content: The page contains no information relevant to the postconditions of the 'Terminate and Purge Surveillance Tracks' use case. The text describes filter settings for J7.6 messages (Reference Points, EW product information, Geographic Area Filters) and specifications for Moving Filters, but does not describe the system state resulting from the termination or purging of tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: negative evidence: confirms the absence of specific data regarding the successful completion state of the track termination/purge process on this page.
